CEG.how_it_makes_money: Constellation owns the largest US fleet of nuclear plants and sells the electricity they make, both into wholesale markets and directly to homes and businesses under contracts. Nuclear plants are expensive to build but cheap to run, so when power prices or long-term contract prices are high, most of the extra revenue drops to profit. Federal nuclear tax credits also put a floor under what its plants earn.
CEG.customers: Utilities, grid operators, millions of retail and business customers, and a growing list of tech companies on long-term contracts; the 10-K does not flag any single customer as a large share of revenue.
CEG.ai_exposure: Tech buyers are signing long-term nuclear contracts: a 20-year Microsoft deal backs the restart of the roughly 835 MW Crane plant, and a 20-year Meta contract for Clinton starts in June 2027. Most of that revenue is still in the future; 2025 revenue mostly reflects higher market and retail prices.
watch: First full quarters including Calpine (closed Jan 7, 2026) and how the combined segments are now reported
Progress and timing on the Crane restart for Microsoft
New data center contracts and the prices they lock in
risks: Lower wholesale power prices or weaker PJM capacity auction results would cut margins on uncontracted output
Regulators or grid operators could limit co-locating data centers at plants, slowing new contracts
CEG.notes: FY2025 figures exclude Calpine, which was acquired on Jan 7, 2026, so 2026 revenue will be much larger. The Other line uses the segment-note figure of $3.565B, which already includes about $0.8B of unrealized hedge losses; the MD&A shows Other ($4.37B) and unrealized losses (-$0.805B) separately.

VST.how_it_makes_money: Vistra owns a big fleet of power plants and also runs one of the largest retail electricity businesses in the US. Its plants make power cheaply and its retail brands sell it to households and businesses at a markup, so the two halves hedge each other. Profit comes from the spread between what it costs to make power and what customers and markets pay for it.
VST.customers: Millions of residential and business retail customers, mostly in Texas, plus grid operators and wholesale buyers; no single large customer is disclosed.
VST.ai_exposure: In September 2025 Vistra signed a 20-year contract to supply Amazon Web Services 1,200 MW of carbon-free power from its Comanche Peak nuclear plant. The 10-K cites data centers as a main driver of expected load growth in Texas and PJM.
